title: Adic middle extension and boundary restriction are constructible sheaves
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-wf-middle-extension]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ has characteristic $p$, $k$ is its chosen algebraic closure, and $\ell\ne p$ is prime with chosen algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $C_0$ be a separated finite-type smooth $k_0$-scheme of pure dimension one, let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion, and let $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be the reduced closed complement. Write $C,U,Z,j,i$ for their geometric base changes to $k$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $U_0$, with lisse adic sheaves and ordinary sheaf direct image interpreted as in [def-wf-middle-extension], and Weil structure as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Put $A=j_*\mathcal F$, the ordinary sheaf direct image, and $B=i^*A$, where $i^*$ is the inverse-image operation of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Here the induced Weil structure on $A$ is the composite of $j_*$ of the Weil structure of $\mathcal F$ with the canonical isomorphism $Lg_C^*j_*\mathcal F\cong j_*Lg_U^*\mathcal F$, which holds because the geometric Frobenius automorphism $g_C$ of $C$ restricts to the automorphism $g_U$ of $U$, and the induced Weil structure on $B$ is $i^*$ of it, using $g_C\circ i=i\circ g_Z$.

Then $A$, with its induced Weil structure, is an object of the constructible heart $\Sh_c(C,\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-constructible-heart], and $B$, with its induced Weil structure, is an object of $\Sh_c(Z,\Qlb)$. In both assertions the ordinary coefficient sheaf is placed in degree zero; no replacement of $j_*\mathcal F$ by the full complex $Rj_*\mathcal F$ is made.

source.place: Proof, first sentence (constructible input K=j_*F) and finite-boundary sentence (constructibility of i^*j_*F); the coefficient interpretation is def-wf-middle-extension

proof.text: First check the geometric hypotheses. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $C$ is separated and finite type over $k$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), its structure morphism is smooth of relative dimension one, as is that of $C_0$. For the projection $p_C:C\to C_0$, [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ over $k_0$ says that $p_C$ is open. Every nonempty open $W\subset C$ has nonempty open image meeting the dense $U_0$; a point in that intersection lifts to $W\cap p_C^{-1}(U_0)$. Thus $U$ is dense in $C$. Forget the Weil structure temporarily and use the geometric immersion pair $j:U\hookrightarrow C$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$ in the statement. In the finite-coefficient-field adic category, [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] explicitly says that ordinary open direct image sends lisse sheaves on $U$ to constructible sheaves on $C$. Apply this to the underlying lisse sheaf $\mathcal F$. The sheaf obtained is precisely $A=j_*\mathcal F$ of [def-wf-middle-extension], whose direct-image convention is ordinary sheaf pushforward, not the entire derived image. The same cohomology interface identifies the standard heart with constructible sheaves, so $A[0]$ belongs to $\Sh_c(C,\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-constructible-heart]. The interface assumes a smooth separated finite-type curve over a perfect field and a dense open; here it is applied on the geometric curve over $k$, with exactly those hypotheses. It requires neither connectedness nor properness.

source.place: First sentence, K=j_*F; constructible input supplied by the existing rational open–closed cohomology interface

proof.text: By [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], the constructible pullback $i^*$ for this complementary immersion pair is t-exact. Thus it sends $A[0]$, which is in both standard halves, into both standard halves on $Z$. The same node identifies these halves and their heart with ordinary cohomology of pro-etale coefficient-module representatives. Consequently this object is the degree-zero ordinary inverse image $B=i^*A$ in the conventions of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and it lies in $\Sh_c(Z,\Qlb)$ by [def-weil-constructible-heart]. This deduction uses the adic interface itself, not finite-ring constructibility of a boundary stalk.

source.place: §6.8, Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.8, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; applied through lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology

proof.text: Write $\theta: Lg_U^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$ for the given Weil isomorphism. Since $g_C$ is an automorphism restricting to $g_U$, reindexing site objects by these automorphisms gives a natural isomorphism $c:Lg_C^*j_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}j_*Lg_U^*\mathcal F$: the two section formulas identify by the isomorphism between pulling a neighborhood back by $g_C$ and then intersecting with $U$, and first intersecting with $U$ and pulling back by $g_U$. Restrictions and coefficient actions agree under that fiber-product identification; the inverse uses the inverse automorphisms. On the adic common-stage categories these are the same cohomology comparisons, compatible with coefficient extension and Frobenius, stated in [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology]. Hence $\theta_A=(j_*\theta)\circ c$ is an isomorphism $Lg_C^*A\to A$. The equality $g_Ci=ig_Z$ similarly gives $b:Lg_Z^*i^*A\xrightarrow{\sim}i^*Lg_C^*A$; put $\theta_B=i^*(\theta_A)\circ b$. Functors preserve inverses, so $\theta_B$ is an isomorphism. Scheme isomorphisms preserve the standard structure by the cited interface. Thus these are isomorphisms on the two heart objects already obtained, and [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], clause 3, makes $(A,\theta_A)$ and $(B,\theta_B)$ constructible Weil sheaves. They are exactly the induced structures specified in the statement.

lean.note: The main theorem states heart-carrier membership of the actual fixed pairs with induced Weil structures. Helpers form the reduced closed complement by its vanishing ideal, realize the recorded lisse system and ordinary image at its literal finite stage, and normalize immersion pullback and Frobenius squares on module-unit generators, Roos coordinates and K-flat representatives. The induced open-image isomorphism is selected only from a unique ordinary-counit characterization; the boundary structure is its actual inverse-image composite.
